name: linux_lars
tag: have you tried ubuntu? no really. i have a cd. i have 40 cds. take one
blogTitle: uptime: a log of things that work on my machine
about: hi. i'm lars. i run linux [0]. i compiled my own kernel twice this week, once on purpose. it took me three days to get the wifi working on this thinkpad and those were the three best days of my summer, because nobody handed it to me. i did it. me and a forum post from a stranger named penguin_dad. that is called freedom. your computer came with an operating system somebody else picked for you, and i'm not judging, i'm just standing here holding a free ubuntu cd. i ordered 40. they mail them to you for nothing. sound doesn't work on my machine yet, but honestly the internet was too loud anyway. --- [0] GNU/Linux, technically. i'll stop. i won't stop.
aboutMore: full disclosure, since openness is the whole idea: there is a 4gb windows partition on this laptop. it exists for exactly one program, a roller coaster game from my childhood that will not run any other way. the partition is named SHAME. i boot it maybe once a month, build one wooden coaster, and leave. also: my nana runs ubuntu now. i set it up in june. she plays solitaire, emails me in all lowercase, and has had zero viruses, which she has told her entire church.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: penguin_dad from the forums, who posted the wifi fix at 4am and never posted again. linus torvalds (i'd just nod). whoever puts the free cds in the envelopes, to apologize for ordering 40. and one person on this site who will say 'ok lars, install it' and mean it. dave doesn't count. dave has been 'about to' since spring.

interests.General: linux, compiling things, recompiling things, config files, the terminal, forum threads from strangers, handing out cds, dual-booting (don't ask), thinkpads, taking the long way on principle, sunday dinner at nana's
interests.Music: whatever plays in my head (see: sound card). back when it worked: daft punk, kraftwerk, jonathan coulton, they might be giants, video game soundtracks in .ogg (not mp3. ask me why) (please ask me why)
interests.Movies: hackers (inaccurate. i own it), the matrix, office space, antitrust (so bad. seen it 6 times), wargames, tron, revolution os (a documentary about operating systems. i got a little emotional at the end)
interests.Television: i don't have a tv card that works under linux. at nana's on sundays: wheel of fortune. otherwise mythbusters, futurama, the screen savers (rest in peace)
interests.Books: the man pages, the cathedral and the bazaar, just for fun (linus's book), the 'wireless troubleshooting' sticky on the ubuntu forums (47 pages, read twice), the hitchhiker's guide to the galaxy
interests.Heroes: linus torvalds, penguin_dad, tux, my nana (my only successful install on another human's computer), todd (runs a whole site off one laptop. on the wrong operating system. but still.)

nana says hi. she emailed me that. from ubuntu. unprompted.
thanksAdd: connection established :) thanks for the add. quick question, no pressure: what operating system are you on right now. you don't have to answer. i can tell from how the page looks. i have a cd for you whenever you're ready. it's free. it's always been free.
ambient: recompiled the kernel without joystick support. saved 40 kilobytes. boot time is down 0.2 seconds. i own no joysticks. worth it.
uptime: 31 days. this laptop has been on longer than some of your relationship statuses.
gave out 3 ubuntu cds at lunch. one is now a coaster, one is a frisbee, and one is in a computer. 33% conversion. i'll take it.
sound worked for 11 minutes last night. i don't know what i did. i heard one (1) startup drum and then silence again. i'm choosing to see it as a visit.
nana emailed to say solitaire 'froze.' she had just won. the cards do a little thing when you win. she thought she broke it. she's 14 and 0 this week.
three days for wifi. people say that like it's bad. you know how long it took you? zero days. and what did you learn? exactly.
saltyDm: request denied. ok. 'permission denied' is a normal part of life on linux, i see it forty times a day, usually from my own computer. i'll just try again as root. (that's a joke.) (the cd offer stands.)

keywords.linux: have you tried it? i have a cd. it's free, it's legal, and it comes with 16,000 programs, four of which i can get working. i can walk you through the install. clear your weekend. and the one after.
keywords.windows: i'm not going to say anything negative. i'm going to say 'blue screen' in a calm voice and let you sit with it. (yes i have a windows partition. it's 4gb. it's named SHAME. we've been over this.)
keywords.wifi: three days. a broadcom chip, a program that wraps a windows driver in a linux blanket, and a 4am post from a stranger called penguin_dad. when the little bars lit up i stood up in my room. alone. arms raised.
keywords.mac: it's unix underneath. i keep telling miles. he has a terminal and he has never opened it. it's like owning a piano and using it as a shelf.
keywords.ubuntu: it's an old word meaning 'i can't configure debian.' that's a joke we tell. i tell. alone. do you want a cd
keywords.sound: sound has not worked since august. i've read every thread. at this point i think of it as a feature. the internet is very calm in here.

miles: miles you paid $1,299 for a computer with one mouse button. i paid $0 for my operating system and i have three buttons AND a little red nub. do the math.
miles. we agreed never to bring up the coffee shop. yes i borrowed your macbook to look up the wifi fix. for nine minutes. i washed my hands after. it changes nothing.
dave: dave. status check on the install. the cd i burned you is from april. there's been a whole new version since. it's fine. the old one still works. it's waiting. like me.
dave you told kevin you 'run a dual boot.' you run windows and a cd in a drawer. that's not a dual boot, that's a hope.
todd: todd, respectfully: what is the server running. you said 'the one it came with.' todd. TODD. i can have it on debian by sunday. you'd never go down again [0]. --- [0] you'd go down for the whole weekend first
todd the site dropped for 20 minutes at 7pm again. was it the vacuum. i wrote you a script that emails you when the laptop gets unplugged. it can't send while unplugged. i see the flaw now.
larry: larry. 'ubuntu_FULL.exe' is not ubuntu. ubuntu is 700 megabytes and comes on the cd that I HANDED YOU. what you installed is a toolbar with a penguin on it. that penguin is an impostor.
larry let me wipe it. one afternoon. your 400 viruses can't even run on linux. they'd just stand around confused. you'd be free. the gorilla can't come. i'm sorry. i know.
doug: doug how's the text browser. remember: arrow keys to move, enter to follow a link, and you never have to load a glitter gif again. you're the fastest guy on dial-up in the county now.
doug i did the math. downloading ubuntu would take you 28 hours with zero phone calls. so i mailed you a cd. it'll get there before the first percent would have.
angela: angela in a text browser your front page is 31 picture placeholders and one sentence. the sentence is 'welcome to my site, please be patient while it loads.' i found that very honest.
angela i ran your page through a validator. 212 errors. it also said 'this page uses frames' in a way that sounded worried about you. i fixed nothing. it's your art. but i know now.
dmitri: dmitri 9 frames per second is technically a slideshow, i'll give you that. but it was MY slideshow. nobody sold it to me.
dmitri next LAN i'm bringing the thinkpad again. i've got it up to 14 fps if i turn off the walls. i don't need walls. i know where they are.

bulletins.subject: FREE CDS (not music) (better than music) (it's an operating system)
bulletins.body: i have 31 ubuntu cds left. they're free. they were free to me too: a company mails them to you if you ask, which i did, possibly too enthusiastically. each one comes in a little cardboard sleeve with people holding hands on it. you can try it without installing anything. put it in, restart, and it runs off the cd. your files are safe. your toolbars are safe (larry). if you hate it, take it out and it never happened. if you love it, find me. i'm the one at the lunch table with a thinkpad and no audio. current takers: nana (installed), todd (on a shelf), miles (coaster), dave (drawer). be the fifth. be the second real one. -- lars

bulletins.subject: survey: how long did it take YOU
bulletins.body: copy, paste, be honest. 1) how long did it take you to get on the internet today? 2) did you have to edit a text file to do it? 3) did you learn anything? 4) do you know what your wireless card is called? its real name? 5) do you feel free? my answers: 1) four seconds (today. in june: three days). 2) not today. 3) every day. 4) broadcom bcm4306. we've been through a lot. 5) yes. also tired. mostly yes.

confession: i booted the SHAME partition tonight. built a wooden roller coaster with a 62 mph drop. named it 'kernel panic.' the little people loved it. i felt nothing. (i felt a lot.)
{you} can you hear the song on my profile? is it good? i picked it in july, when sound still worked. i have never actually heard it play on my own page.
someone at school asked me to fix their computer and i said 'have you tried ubuntu' and they said 'i just need to print.' i said 'me too, man.' we stood there for a while.

blog.title: three days: the wifi log
blog.body: day 1, 2pm. fresh install. no wireless. the card is a broadcom, which the forums describe as 'a journey.' day 1, 9pm. found a program that lets linux wear a windows driver like a coat. i need the windows driver. it's on the internet. i don't have internet. that's the problem i'm solving. day 2, noon. walked the laptop to the coffee shop. borrowed a computer from someone there [0] to put the driver on a usb stick. day 2, midnight. driver loads. card lights up. no networks found. i can see the router from my chair. day 3, 4am. a forum user named penguin_dad says there's a second driver fighting the first one. two drivers, one card, like raccoons in a trash can. removed one. the bars lit up. i stood. i raised my arms. i woke up my mom. she said 'is it the internet again.' yes, mom. it is. --- [0] it was miles. it was a macbook. this never leaves the footnote.

blog.title: install report: nana (success)
blog.body: subject: one (1) grandmother, age 74, previously running windows with a weather toolbar and a kitten screensaver she believed was a tv channel. install date: a sunday in june. duration: 40 minutes, plus dinner. everything worked on the first try, including sound, which i am not bitter about. training: i showed her the browser, the email and solitaire. she asked where the kittens went. i found her new kittens. ninety days later: zero viruses. zero toolbars. she emails me every morning ('lars the computer is good today'). she is 14 and 0 at solitaire this week because she discovered undo and considers it legal. last sunday her friend dolores asked what kind of computer it was and nana said 'it's a linux. my grandson put freedom on it.' i have converted exactly one person in two years and it's the best one. i go back every sunday. the computer never needs fixing. i go anyway.
